literal: For striking the bandits without advancing, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.
idiomatic: Because he failed to press the attack, he was stripped of office and rank and sent to the frontier.

literal: Gaozu again, because Yi had shown merit in the former dynasty, summoned him as Grand Inner Custodian.
idiomatic: Gaozu, remembering Yi's merit under the former emperor, recalled him as grand inner custodian.

literal: In the first year of Tian'an he died.
idiomatic: He died in Tian'an year 1.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns West and Prince of Jian'an; posthumous title Kang.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who campaigns west and prince of Jian'an, with the posthumous title Kang.

literal: His son Jisheng inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jisheng succeeded.

literal: Jisheng's younger brother Li, Liangzhou garrison commander and Duke Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: Jisheng's brother Li was Liangzhou garrison commander and duke who pacifies the south.

literal: His son Qi, courtesy name Yuande.
idiomatic: His son Qi, styled Yuande.

literal: Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Administrator of Shanggu and Hanoi commanderies, Secretariat Aide of Si Province, Crown Prince Right Guard Leader.
idiomatic: He served as regular attendant of direct communication, administrator of Shanggu and Hanoi, secretariat aide of Si Province, and crown prince right guard leader.

literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Qi Province.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made inspector of Qi Province.

literal: His son Jingxiang, courtesy name Badu.
idiomatic: His son Jingxiang, styled Badu.

literal: Secretariat Attendant, Administrator of Shangdang.
idiomatic: He was secretariat attendant and administrator of Shangdang.

literal: Li's younger brother Nigan, held Central Protocol Regiment lieutenant and was granted the title Baron of Lin'an.
idiomatic: Li's brother Nigan was a central protocol regiment lieutenant and was enfeoffed baron of Lin'an.

literal: Later he gradually held eminent posts; made Inspector of Ji Province, acting General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: He later rose through eminent posts, became inspector of Ji Province, and held acting rank as general who pacifies the south and duke of Julu.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Hun inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Hun inherited the title.

literal: Secretariat Archivist.
idiomatic: He was secretariat archivist.

literal: His son Lingxuan, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
idiomatic: His son Lingxuan was regular attendant of direct communication.

literal: Chong's clansman Chou Shan, at the beginning of Taizu, led his division in submission and, with Chong, joined hearts and shared strength to defend left and right.
idiomatic: Chong's clansman Chou Shan, in Taizu's early reign, led his following in to submit and, with Chong, fought side by side at the ruler's left and right.

literal: He followed campaigns against Kuduo and Liu Xian and defeated and pacified them.
idiomatic: He followed the campaigns against Kuduo and Liu Xian and broke and pacified them.

literal: He also followed in striking the Helan tribe and pacified the Kumoxi.
idiomatic: He also followed in attacking the Helan and pacified the Kumoxi.

literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.
idiomatic: He was made grandee of the heavenly division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Moti, following in pacifying the Central Plains, was Administrator of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: His son Moti, after helping pacify the central plains, was administrator of Zhongshan.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou, acting Marquis of Yangling.
idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, with acting rank as marquis of Yangling.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Tu, in Taizong's time, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: His son Tu was regular attendant of scattered cavalry under Taizong.

literal: He died while holding Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: He died while serving as palace attendant and general who pacifies the east.

literal: His son Dun, General Who Assists the State and Western Frontier Commander.
idiomatic: His son Dun was general who assists the state and western frontier commander.

literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Fuping.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed viscount of Fuping.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Chun inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Chun inherited the title.

literal: He served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Palace Residence.
idiomatic: He was regular attendant of scattered cavalry and director of the palace residence.

literal: In Gaozong's time he was Right Guard General; shortly made Right General and Inspector of He Province.
idiomatic: Under Gaozong he was right guard general, then right general and inspector of He Province.

literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Bing Province.

literal: His son Sheng inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Sheng inherited the title.

literal: Direct-Palace General.
idiomatic: He was direct-palace general.

literal: Sheng's younger brother Yu, General Who Assists the State and Palace Scribe.
idiomatic: Sheng's brother Yu was general who assists the state and palace scribe.

literal: Yu's son Li, Administrator of Dongmou.
idiomatic: Yu's son Li was administrator of Dongmou.

literal: Li's younger brother Lue, at the end of Wuding, Vice Director of the capital Intendant's office.
idiomatic: Li's brother Lue, at the end of Wuding, was vice director under the capital intendant.

literal: Chun's younger brother Sa, served as Eastern Palace Vice Prefect and Administrator of Ji commandery.
idiomatic: Chun's brother Sa was eastern palace vice prefect and administrator of Ji commandery.

literal: In Shizong's time he was made Garrison Commander of Huaishuo, Eastern and Northern Central Commander, and Inspector of Bin, You, and Liang provinces.
idiomatic: Under Shizong he was garrison commander of Huaishuo, eastern and northern central commander, and inspector of Bin, You, and Liang provinces.

literal: In Suzong's time he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing Province, and Grandee of the Golden Crown and Purple Radiance.
idiomatic: Under Suzong he was made general who pacifies the north, inspector of Bing Province, and grandee of the golden crown and purple radiance.

literal: In office he was famed for fierce might.
idiomatic: In office he was famed for fierce might.

literal: He died at age seventy-four; posthumously made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Campaigns East, Inspector of Xiangzhou; posthumous title An.
idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously made regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who campaigns east, and inspector of Xiangzhou, with the posthumous title An.

literal: His son Xianshou, Colonel of the Long River.
idiomatic: His son Xianshou was colonel of the long river.

literal: Xianshou's younger brother Xianye died while holding Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: Xianshou's brother Xianye died as regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

literal: Zilin's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Xiande.
idiomatic: Zilin's younger brother Liang, styled Xiande.

literal: Bureau Aide in the Directorate of Works, Director of Palace Construction, Libationer of the Masters of Writing, General Who Pacifies the East, Administrator of Southern Julu.
idiomatic: He was directorate of works bureau aide, director of palace construction, libationer of the masters of writing, general who pacifies the east, and administrator of southern Julu.

literal: He had considerable repute among the people.
idiomatic: He enjoyed considerable repute among the people.

literal: He entered service as Masters of Writing Marshal, Staff Supervisor of the Grand General, and Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: He entered the capital as masters of writing marshal, staff supervisor of the grand general, and secretariat attendant.

literal: He died in the sixth year of Wuding.
idiomatic: He died in Wuding year 6.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Xu Province.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who campaigns east and inspector of Xu Province.

literal: The historiographer writes: From of old Mu Chong served the dragon countenance, early showed loyal devotion, and so received favor to the summit of the secretariat;
idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Mu Chong long served the throne, showed early loyalty, and rose to the secretariat's peak;

literal: he even took part in treasonous plotting yet in the end was wholly spared — how thick is an enlightened lord's treatment of his toiling servants!
idiomatic: he even joined treason yet was spared in the end — how generous is an enlightened ruler toward a weary servant!

literal: To share sacrifice in the temple court also honored the principle of valuing merit.
idiomatic: Sharing the temple sacrifice likewise honored merit above all.

literal: Guan in youth was fit for ministerial office — were his talents and capacity not outstanding?
idiomatic: Guan in youth was fit for the highest offices — were his talent and bearing not outstanding?

literal: Yi was fierce and illustrious; Liang reached rank through generous breadth; Shao upheld unadorned simplicity; Bi bore a name for style — generation on generation they did not fall, purple and blue offices filling the rolls — how grand!
idiomatic: Yi blazed with martial fame; Liang rose through generous breadth; Shao kept unadorned simplicity; Bi won a name for style — generation after generation the house did not decline, purple and blue rank filling the rolls — how grand!

literal: As for Shou, he ended in wealth and rank; Pi alone was stripped and reduced — men's lack of propriety makes good fortune all the more common.
idiomatic: Shou died in wealth and rank; Pi alone was stripped and reduced — when men abandon propriety, luck counts for more.

literal: Chou's descendants too were not lacking in fame and rank — they also had their men!
idiomatic: Chou's descendants too held name and rank — the line also had its men!

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Textual notes

literal: "Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu to respond": in various editions and Beishi juan 20, Biography of Mu Chong, "Huan" all reads "Zhi."
idiomatic: "Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu to join them": editions and Beishi juan 20, Mu Chong's life, all read Huan (桓) as Zhi (植).

literal: Cefu juan 134
idiomatic: Cefu, juan 134

literal: 〈page 1616〉
idiomatic: folio 1616

literal: reads "Huan."
idiomatic: has "Huan."

literal: Commentary: Juan 2, Annals of Taizu, recording this affair, has the patchwork and Southern editions reading "Huan" and other editions reading "Zhi."
idiomatic: Note: Taizu's annals, juan 2, on this affair have patchwork and Southern texts with Huan and other editions with Zhi.

literal: Beishi juan 1, Annals of Wei 1, this book, and Beishi juan 15, Biography of Kuduo, all read "Huan."
idiomatic: Beishi juan 1 (Wei annals 1), this book, and Beishi juan 15 (Kuduo) all have Huan.

literal: This Cefu entry was taken from the Mu Chong biography, yet it too reads "Huan."
idiomatic: This Cefu entry comes from Mu Chong's life yet also reads Huan.

literal: Knowing the character "Zhi" is erroneous, the text is now emended according to Cefu.
idiomatic: Zhi is a corruption; the text is emended per Cefu.

literal: The same below.
idiomatic: The same below; not listed again.

literal: "As a frontier subject his loyal submission was long manifest": in various editions "kuan" (submission) reads "jiao" (teach).
idiomatic: "As a frontier subject his loyal submission was long manifest": editions read kuan (submission) as jiao (teach).

literal: Cefu juan 353
idiomatic: Cefu, juan 353

literal: 〈page 4192〉
idiomatic: folio 4192

literal: reads "kuan."
idiomatic: has "kuan" (submission).

literal: Commentary: "kuan" means "kuanfu" (submission) and "chengkuan" (sincere submission) — that is, as a "frontier subject" his "loyal" attitude was long manifest; the character "jiao" is erroneous and is now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: Note: kuan means loyal submission as a frontier subject; jiao is a corruption and is emended accordingly.

literal: "Summoned as Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": Beishi juan 20 has "right" as "left."
idiomatic: "Summoned as palace attendant and right vice director of the masters of writing": Northern History juan 20 reads right as left.

literal: Commentary: Juan 7, upper, Annals of Gaozu, fourth month of the twelfth year of Taihe and twelfth month both record "Left Vice Director Mu Liang."
idiomatic: Note: Gaozu's annals, juan 7 upper, Taihe year 12, months 4 and 12, both record "left vice director Mu Liang."

literal: It is suspected that "left" is correct.
idiomatic: Left is likely correct.

literal: "Therefore I humble you to bring glory to it": in the Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau four editions "guang" (glory) reads "xian" (before); the patchwork and Ji editions read "guang."
idiomatic: "Therefore I humble you to bring glory to it": Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions read guang (glory) as xian (before); patchwork and Ji have guang.

literal: Commentary: This says Mu Guan was to be national university assistant; in that office there was glory — now follow the patchwork edition.
idiomatic: Note: Mu Guan was to be national university assistant, an office that brought honor; the patchwork reading is followed.

literal: "Selected as Kingdom Chamberlain for Prince of Guangping Huai": in various editions "Guang" reads "Gao"; Beishi juan 20 reads "Guang."
idiomatic: "Selected as kingdom chamberlain for Prince of Guangping Huai": editions read Guang (廣) as Gao (高); Northern History juan 20 has Guang.

literal: Commentary: Prince of Guangping Huai has biographies in this book juan 22 and Beishi juan 19; the character "Gao" is clearly erroneous and is now emended accordingly.
idiomatic: Note: Prince of Guangping Huai has lives in this book juan 22 and Beishi juan 19; Gao is clearly wrong and is emended accordingly.

literal: "The Qiang of He Province, Que Tiecong, rebelled": in various editions "cong" reads "hu"; juan 9, Annals of Suzong, first year of Shengui, and juan 105, part 4, Monograph on Astronomy 4, recording this affair, all read "cong."
idiomatic: "The Qiang of He Province, Que Tiecong, rebelled": editions read cong (怱) as hu (忽); Suzong annals juan 9, Shengui year 1, and Astronomy monograph juan 105.4 all have cong.

literal: Juan 41, Biography of Yuan He with attached Biography of Yuan Zigong, reads "hu," while Beishi juan 28, Biography of Yuan Zigong, reads "cong."
idiomatic: Juan 41, Yuan He with attached Yuan Zigong, has hu; Beishi juan 28, Yuan Zigong, has cong.

literal: Commentary: Que Tiecong was a Qiang personal name.
idiomatic: Note: Que Tiecong was a Qiang man's name.

literal: The Zhou shu three-dynasty edition repeatedly has "Pangqi Tiecong," and the Palace edition also often corrupts it to "hu."
idiomatic: The Zhou shu three-dynasty text repeatedly has "Pangqi Tiecong," and the Palace edition also often corrupts this to hu.

literal: Now emended according to the annals.
idiomatic: Emended per the annals.

literal: "The lord of the Azhi Luo state, Fuluo Yueju, was broken by the Rouran": the patchwork edition reads "A" as "He," other editions as "He," Cefu juan 728
idiomatic: "The Azhi Luo lord Fuluo Yueju was broken by the Rouran": patchwork reads A (阿) as He (河); other editions as He (何); Cefu juan 728

literal: 〈page 8660〉
idiomatic: folio 8660

literal: reads "A."
idiomatic: has "A" (Azhi).

literal: Commentary: Beishi juan 6, Annals of Qi, upper, Beishi juan 1, Annals of Divine Martiality, upper
idiomatic: Note: Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, upper), Beishi juan 1 (Divine Martiality, upper)

literal: 〈supplement〉
idiomatic: supplement

literal: Yongxi year 2, and juan 2, Annals of Divine Martiality, lower
idiomatic: Yongxi year 2, and juan 2 (Divine Martiality, lower)

literal: 〈supplement〉
idiomatic: supplement

literal: Wuding year 3 all record "Azhi Luo"; now emended according to Cefu.
idiomatic: Wuding year 3 all have "Azhi Luo"; emended per Cefu.
